title: Exos API
description: A REST API over one organization's Exos data: events, ticket types, add-ons, promo codes, attendees and tickets, door scans and check-in, guest lists, orders, invoices, refunds, refund requests, comps, disputes, payouts, fans, tags and webhooks (core writes run the same rules as the dashboard: each runs as the member who created the key, needs that member's role in the organization and is logged); tickets sold on other platforms (sales counts), booking (venues, rooms, holds, the show schedule, staff notes and contacts), offers, budgets and offer pools, deals, finance items, settlements, profit and loss and ticket-count emails, artists and lineups to read and write; plus a public listing feed for listing sites. Use it to sync sales into a CRM or a spreadsheet, show your events on your own site, feed Bandsintown or JamBase, run a box office, a door app or booking from your own tools, or build reports. Every request is scoped to the organization of the key that makes it. Reads are GET; writes are POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE with a JSON (or form-encoded) body and need a `:write` scope (listing-feed shared keys: `org:admin`). Responses are JSON, and times are ISO 8601 strings in UTC. Paths below are relative to the base URL (the exos-api edge function of your Supabase project), e.g. https://<project-ref>.supabase.co/functions/v1/exos-api/v1/events. Each path also answers without the /v1 prefix, for clients of the first release. Call the API from your server: it sends no CORS headers (the listing feed does), and a key in a browser is a key anyone can copy.

authentication.description: Send an organization API key as a bearer token. An owner or manager creates keys in Org settings → Developer, choosing the scopes each key gets; the key (sk_live_ plus 48 hex characters) is shown once, and only its SHA-256 hash and a 16-character prefix are stored. An organization has at most 10 active keys. Keys do not expire: they work until revoked, and a key is revoked automatically when the member who created it leaves the organization. A request for anything outside the key's organization answers 404, so ids from other organizations cannot be probed.
authentication.token_validity: API keys do not expire; revoke one in Org settings when it is no longer needed.

methods.name: Organization API key
methods.description: Every endpoint except the public listing feed. Held to the scopes chosen when the key was created (an owner or manager can change them later). Keys created before scopes existed carry the legacy `read` scope, which covers every `:read` scope.

methods.name: Listing-feed shared key
methods.description: The public listing feed only (/v1/public/events and /v1/public/confirms). One key per listing partner (Bandsintown, JamBase, Songkick, your website, other), minted by an org owner in Org settings → Listing feed or with POST /v1/listing-keys. It reads that organization's public events and nothing else, carries no scopes, and tags ticket links with the partner (utm_source). sh_live_ plus 48 hex characters, shown once; only its SHA-256 hash and a 16-character prefix are stored. At most 20 active keys per organization; revoking one takes effect at once.

authentication.scopes_description: Every API-key endpoint needs one scope, named on the endpoint; GET /v1/me needs none, and the shared-key feed has no scopes. Reads need a `:read` scope and writes a `:write` scope; artists and lineups use `events:read` / `events:write`, listing-feed keys need `org:admin`. A key without the scope gets 403 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope". A `:write` scope covers the `:read` scope of the same resource, and the legacy `read` scope covers every `:read` scope. The `:write` scopes without routes can already be granted, so a key can be narrowed ahead of the routes that will use them. `refunds:write` is the only scope that can refund, and no other scope implies it. GET /v1/me returns a key's scopes as stored and as they take effect.

pagination.description: List endpoints marked as paged take page and per_page and answer { data, meta }. meta.total is the number of rows matching the filters and meta.total_pages the number of pages at this per_page; walk the list by asking for page + 1 until page >= total_pages. A page past the end answers an empty data array. Each list has a fixed order (documented per endpoint) with a tiebreak on the id, so pages do not overlap while the data is unchanged. Endpoints that are not paged answer { data: [...] } with every row. A bad page or per_page answers 400.

rate_limiting.description: 120 requests per API key per clock minute (a fixed one-minute window), counted for every authenticated request, errors included. Over the limit the answer is 429 { "error": "rate limit exceeded", "limit_per_minute": 120 } with a Retry-After header: the seconds until the next minute starts. If the rate limiter itself is unavailable the request is refused with 503 and Retry-After: 30, because the API returns personal data and is never served unmetered.

limits.limit: 120 requests a minute per API key

error_format.description: Errors are JSON with a human-readable error message. Some carry a little more: 403 names the scope that was needed, 429 the limit, and 404 for an unknown path a hint.

error_codes.name: Not modified
error_codes.description: Listing feed only: the If-None-Match header names the current ETag, so the response has no body.

error_codes.name: Bad request
error_codes.description: A bad page, per_page or filter value, a bad or unknown field in a write body (core writes refuse server-owned fields such as status or sold rather than ignore them), a body that is not JSON, a malformed Idempotency-Key, or an Idempotency-Key already used for another request; the message names it.

error_codes.name: Payment refused
error_codes.description: A refund Stripe refused; nothing was refunded.

error_codes.name: Unauthorized
error_codes.description: No bearer key ("missing bearer API key"), or a key that is unknown or revoked ("invalid or revoked API key").

error_codes.name: Forbidden
error_codes.description: The key lacks the endpoint's scope: the body names it (required_scope) and so does the WWW-Authenticate header: Bearer error="insufficient_scope", scope="…". For a write, also: the member who created the key can't do it in the dashboard (their role), or has left the organization.

error_codes.name: Not found
error_codes.description: An unknown path, or an event or order that does not exist in the key's organization.

error_codes.name: Method not allowed
error_codes.description: A method the path does not answer (e.g. DELETE /v1/holds), or one the API does not answer at all (it answers GET, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE; the listing feed GET and HEAD). The Allow header lists the ones it does.

error_codes.name: Conflict
error_codes.description: A write that clashes with existing data: an event with publish blockers (the body lists them), a tag or fan email that already exists, a daily limit, a ticket type or add-on that has sales, a promo code that exists, a full guest list, a guest who already arrived; renaming a sales count to a label its event already has; a booking write that clashes with what is there (the same room and date twice on one hold, a night that is no longer active, a permalink in use, a second doors row, a limit reached, or deleting a venue or room that hold nights point at); a taken artist permalink, merging an artist that was already merged (or into one), or the 20-active-shared-key limit.

error_codes.name: Payload too large
error_codes.description: A request body over the limit: 64 KB, or 2 MB of CSV for a sales-count import.

error_codes.name: Unsupported media type
error_codes.description: A POST, PUT or PATCH whose Content-Type is neither JSON (application/json) nor form-encoded.

error_codes.name: Unprocessable
error_codes.description: A CSV import whose file has errors; each is listed with its line and field, and nothing was written.

error_codes.name: Too many requests
error_codes.description: Over 120 requests this minute for this key; wait Retry-After seconds.

error_codes.name: Server error
error_codes.description: Unexpected. A read is safe to retry, and so are the sales-count writes (a label or a platform's import replaces, never adds) core writes resent with the same Idempotency-Key, and fan / tag writes (tagging twice is one tag; adding a fan twice answers 409); check any other write with a read before retrying it.

error_codes.name: Bad gateway
error_codes.description: A refund Stripe did not answer. Resend it with the same Idempotency-Key: it will not refund twice.

error_codes.name: Unavailable
error_codes.description: The rate limiter could not be reached, so the request was refused (retry after Retry-After seconds); or a refund while payments are switched off.

webhooks.description: Exos can also push: register an HTTPS endpoint in Org settings → Developer and it receives a signed POST for each event type it subscribes to (ticket.created, ticket.checked_in, order.fulfilled, order.refunded, event.published, hold.created, hold.updated, hold.converted). GET /v1/webhooks lists the endpoints.

signature.format: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<X-Exos-Timestamp>.<raw body>" with the endpoint's secret>
signature.description: Compute the HMAC over the raw request body (before parsing the JSON), compare in constant time, and reject timestamps more than 5 minutes old. X-Exos-Delivery is the same on every retry of a delivery: dedupe on it.

headers.name: X-Exos-Delivery
headers.description: The delivery id; the same across retries.

headers.name: X-Exos-Timestamp
headers.description: Unix seconds when this attempt was sent.

webhooks.retries: A delivery that does not get a 2xx is retried with exponential backoff (about 2^attempt minutes, at most 6 hours apart); after 8 attempts it is given up. Redirects are not followed, and only https URLs at public addresses are called.
